cls: Antiprogestin / progesterone-receptor antagonist; glucocorticoid (GR-II) receptor antagonist
pharm: Blocks progesterone (terminates pregnancy; cervical ripening) and cortisol action (Cushing's hyperglycemia)
quick: Abortion: 200 mg once, then misoprostol; Cushing's: 300 mg/day, titrate
Korlym with a meal; abortion regimen per protocol
Abortifacient; contraindicated in Cushing's use except for its abortion indication
Korlym: do not exceed 600 mg/day in impairment
Korlym: do not exceed 600 mg/day; avoid in severe
summary: Mifepristone is a progesterone- and glucocorticoid-receptor antagonist with two distinct FDA-approved uses: (1) Mifeprex - medical termination of intrauterine pregnancy through 70 days gestation (with misoprostol), which carries a boxed warning for serious and sometimes fatal infections and bleeding and is dispensed under a REMS; and (2) Korlym - control of hyperglycemia secondary to endogenous Cushing's syndrome in adults with type 2 diabetes/glucose intolerance who failed or are not candidates for surgery. The Korlym label carries a separate boxed warning that, because of its antiprogestational action, it will cause termination of pregnancy - so pregnancy must be excluded and prevented during treatment.
indications: Medical termination of intrauterine pregnancy through 70 days gestation (with misoprostol) - Mifeprex
Control of hyperglycemia secondary to endogenous Cushing's syndrome in adults with type 2 diabetes/glucose intolerance who failed or are not surgical candidates - Korlym
Cervical ripening / management of early pregnancy loss (off-label/guideline use in some settings)

dosage.d: Mifepristone 200 mg once, then misoprostol 800 mcg buccal 24-48 h later
dosage.n: Mifeprex REMS; follow-up to confirm complete abortion

dosage.d: Increase by 300 mg at intervals of >=2-4 weeks
Up to 1200 mg/day, not exceeding 20 mg/kg/day
dosage.n: Lower max in renal/hepatic impairment (600 mg/day)

admin: Mifeprex: dispensed only through certified prescribers/pharmacies under a REMS; provide patient counseling and follow-up to confirm complete termination
Korlym tablets: take once daily with a meal; swallow whole, do not crush/split
Exclude pregnancy before Korlym and ensure non-hormonal contraception during and 1 month after
Provide instructions on expected bleeding/cramping after the abortion regimen and warning signs of infection
moa: Synthetic steroid that competitively antagonizes progesterone at the progesterone receptor (causing decidual breakdown, cervical softening, and uterine contractility - terminating pregnancy) and antagonizes cortisol at the glucocorticoid (GR-II) receptor (reducing the metabolic effects of excess cortisol in Cushing's, improving hyperglycemia) without lowering cortisol levels.

absolute: Confirmed or suspected ectopic pregnancy or undiagnosed adnexal mass (abortion use)
Hemorrhagic disorders or concurrent anticoagulant therapy

Korlym: pregnancy (will terminate pregnancy); women requiring corticosteroids for life-threatening conditions; endometrial hyperplasia with atypia or endometrial carcinoma; use with strong CYP3A substrates with narrow therapeutic range
relative: Renal or hepatic impairment (limit Korlym dose)
Concurrent CYP3A inhibitors (limit Korlym to 300 mg/day)

preg: Mifepristone is an abortifacient: it terminates pregnancy. For Cushing's (Korlym) use it is contraindicated in pregnancy and pregnancy must be excluded before treatment and prevented with non-hormonal contraception during and for 1 month after stopping (boxed warning). After medical abortion, contraception can be started promptly per protocol.
lact: Limited data; mifepristone is present in human milk in small amounts. For single-dose abortion use, breastfeeding can generally continue or be briefly interrupted per local guidance. For chronic Korlym use, avoid breastfeeding.
renal: Korlym: in renal impairment, do not exceed 600 mg/day. Use clinical judgment for abortion regimen.
hepatic: Korlym: in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment, do not exceed 600 mg/day; not recommended in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) - markedly increase mifepristone; limit Korlym to 300 mg/day
CYP3A substrates with narrow therapeutic index (e.g., simvastatin, lovastatin, cyclosporine, sirolimus, tacrolimus, fentanyl, ergot alkaloids) - mifepristone inhibits CYP3A; contraindicated/avoid
Long-term corticosteroids - antagonized by mifepristone (Korlym contraindication)
moderate: Strong CYP3A inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's wort) - reduce mifepristone efficacy
QT-prolonging drugs - additive QT risk (Korlym, with hypokalemia)
Hormonal contraceptives - reliability reduced for Korlym; use non-hormonal methods
CYP2C8/2C9 substrates (e.g., warfarin, NSAIDs) - mifepristone may increase levels
minor: Grapefruit juice - may increase mifepristone exposure
interactions.food: Take Korlym with a meal; abortion regimen timing per protocol
interactions.diagnostics: Korlym does not lower serum cortisol/ACTH - these cannot be used to assess efficacy; monitor clinical response and potassium

common: Korlym: nausea, fatigue, headache, hypokalemia, arthralgia, peripheral edema, endometrial thickening
serious: Serious or fatal infection (including atypical/sepsis without fever) - abortion (boxed warning)
Prolonged or heavy uterine bleeding requiring intervention - abortion (boxed warning)
rare: Toxic shock-like syndrome (Clostridium sordellii/perfringens) after abortion
Opportunistic effects of excess CYP3A interactions
emergency: Sepsis/serious infection (severe abdominal pain, weakness, with or without fever, >24 h after misoprostol)

monitoring: Confirmation of complete abortion (clinical, ultrasound, or hCG follow-up)
Signs of infection and excessive bleeding after the regimen
Endometrial monitoring with prolonged Korlym use
counsel: Abortion: expect cramping and bleeding; seek urgent care for soaking 2 pads/hour for 2 hours, severe abdominal pain, weakness, or fever - infection can be life-threatening
Take misoprostol as directed 24-48 hours after mifepristone and attend follow-up
Korlym: take once daily with a meal; do not become pregnant - use a non-hormonal contraceptive
Report severe fatigue, dizziness, nausea/vomiting, or low energy (possible adrenal insufficiency)
Tell all prescribers you take this drug (many drug interactions)
pk: Antiprogestin effect within hours; abortion completed over hours-days with misoprostol
Prolonged receptor effect; once-daily Korlym dosing
pearls: Boxed warning (abortion/Mifeprex): serious and sometimes fatal infection and bleeding; dispensed under a REMS
Korlym boxed warning: will terminate pregnancy - exclude/prevent pregnancy with non-hormonal contraception
Korlym does NOT lower cortisol - blocks its receptor; cortisol/ACTH levels cannot gauge efficacy (monitor clinically and potassium)
Potent CYP3A inhibitor and CYP3A substrate - extensive interaction profile
Atypical sepsis (Clostridium sordellii) after medical abortion may present without fever - maintain high suspicion
missed: Abortion regimen is a single supervised dose - follow clinic instructions and do not self-repeat. For Korlym, take a missed dose as soon as remembered the same day; if it is nearly the next day, skip it and resume the once-daily schedule - do not double up.
overdose: Up to 600 mg single doses have not caused serious adverse effects; very high doses could produce adrenal insufficiency. Management is supportive with monitoring for adrenal insufficiency, hypokalemia, and (in pregnancy use) bleeding. No specific antidote; corticosteroid supplementation may be needed for adrenal insufficiency.
